feature: hex solo — collapse to a single-binary software-engineering agent
description: Execute ADR-2608241500: extract hex-infer so the ReAct loop runs in-process, sever SpacetimeDB, delete the daemon tier (hex-nexus, hex-agent, hex-desktop, hex-state, spacetime-modules, dashboard, SOP pipeline, TUI), triage the CLI down to software-engineering verbs, and trim hex-core to a real contract surface. ~261k LOC to ~49k; 3 processes to 1. The build is already clean at HEAD, so this is ~75% deletion and ~25% extraction. Survey and evidence: docs/analysis/2026-08-24-hex-solo-refactor-plan.md.

phases.name: Ground — baselines and free hygiene
phases.description: Everything in this phase is independent of the collapse decision and reversible or non-destructive. It also establishes the regression oracle for P9. Nothing here touches the daemon, so P0 can land on main before the governance gate. P0.2 is the one destructive task and is operator-gated.

tasks.name: Record P9 baselines
tasks.description: Run `hex bench agentic` over docs/benchmarks/ and record per-model pass-rates to docs/benchmarks/baseline-2608241500.json. Also record: release binary size of target/release/hex (14,159,856 bytes at HEAD), per-crate LOC, transitive dep count per crate (hex-core 34, hex-exec 139, hex-cli 244, hex-nexus 363, workspace 584), and test-function counts (hex-nexus 1000, hex-cli 683, hex-agent 238, hex-core 122, hex-exec 99). These are the only admissible evidence that the collapse did not degrade the loop (S02).

tasks.name: Evict untracked working-tree mass (OPERATOR-GATED)
tasks.description: The repository tracks 2,159 files / 20 MB; the working tree is 31 GB. DO NOT run `git clean -fdx` — it was reviewed on 2026-08-24 and would delete LIVE STATE, not just build output: .hex/adapters/ (126 MB of trained LoRA adapters), .hex/corpus/, .hex/inference/, .hex/state.json, graph-out/ (1.9 MB code knowledge graph), .claude/agents/hex/ (216 KB) and .claude/helpers/, .weave/, hex-agent/.hex/, examples/*/.hex/, examples/research-dashboard/.data/, and every untracked file under docs/ (which includes this workplan, its ADR and its specs). Use a TARGETED allowlist instead: `cargo clean` (target/, 23 GB); rm spacetime-modules/target/ (452 MB); rm examples/*/target/ and examples/*/*/target/ (~931 MB, ebay-clone/backend alone is 508 MB); rm examples/*/node_modules/ (~189 MB); rm hex-nexus/assets/node_modules/ (87 MB) — but NOT hex-nexus/assets/dist/, which rust-embed needs until nexus is deleted in P5.2; rm scripts/lora/__pycache__/. Reclaims ~24.6 GB. Then RELOCATE scripts/lora/.venv/ (5.3 GB Python venv, regenerable from requirements.txt) outside the repository rather than deleting it. Add examples/*/target and examples/*/node_modules to .hexignore. Result: ~1.2 GB working tree, or ~1.1 GB once the venv is moved. Satisfies S13.

tasks.name: Strip 31 foreign skills from .claude/skills
tasks.description: DONE 2026-08-24. Removed the 31 tracked skills belonging to other frameworks — 9 v3-* (claude-flow v3), 5 agentdb-*, 5 github-*, browser, hooks-automation, pair-programming, project-output, reasoningbank-agentdb, reasoningbank-intelligence, skill-builder, sparc-methodology, stream-chain, swarm-advanced, swarm-orchestration, verification-quality (354 KB) — plus the 4 duplicate pairs (hex-adr-create/review/search/status), keeping the dir/SKILL.md form in each case (for hex-adr-create the directory version carried the richer description; the other three were byte-identical). 64 skills -> 29. CORRECTION to the original scope: hex-dashboard, hex-spacetime, hex-publish-module, hex-swarm, hex-dev-rebuild and .claude/agents/neural-lab-researcher.yml were NOT removed here — they document features that still work today, so they are collapse-dependent and belong after the P1 governance gate. Moved to P5.5. Satisfies S11 in part.

tasks.name: Delete dead TypeScript tooling and unwedge hex dev validate
tasks.description: DONE 2026-08-24. src/ and tests/ do not exist (excised by wp-excise-ts-phantom) but package.json was still tracked, declaring bin: dist/cli.js and a test script globbing `tests/unit tests/property tests/smoke`. CORRECTION to the original scope: there is no hardcoded bun step in dev.rs to remove. The real mechanism is `hex dev validate` -> doctor::run_validate_pipeline -> run_tests() at hex-cli/src/commands/doctor/mod.rs:445, which runs `npm test` ONLY IF package.json exists in cwd — correct, generic target-project detection that must stay. Deleting the root package.json IS the entire fix; no Rust change was needed. Deleted package.json, bun.lock (235 KB), tsconfig.json, tsconfig.test.json, eslint.config.js. Four real consumers found by trace and fixed: (1) .github/workflows/ci.yml — removed the `version-check` job (existed only to compare Cargo.toml against package.json; would have hard-failed) and the `build-and-test` job (bun install plus three already-self-skipping steps); neither had dependents. (2) .github/workflows/test.yml — removed the bun install + tsc steps from the lint and unit jobs, renamed 'Lint (clippy + tsc)' to 'Lint (clippy)'. (3) scripts/bump-patch.sh — package.json was the declared single source of truth for the version; flipped to Cargo.toml, verified with --dry-run (reads 26.5.1 correctly). (4) scripts/release.sh — dropped the package.json lockstep block and removed it from `git add`. hex-nexus/assets/package.json (the dashboard's) left untouched — it is live until P5.2. Gate: `cargo check --workspace --exclude hex-desktop` = 0 errors. Satisfies S12.

tasks.name: Drop hex-desktop from workspace members
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. hex-desktop removed from [workspace] members. `cargo check --workspace` now returns 0 errors with no --exclude needed.

ORIGINAL: hex-desktop is the only crate failing the workspace build, and it fails on missing SYSTEM libraries (gdk-3.0, dbus-1) rather than code — taking `cargo check --workspace` down with it and creating the impression that the workspace is broken. Remove it from [workspace] members in Cargo.toml. One line; it is deleted outright in P5.3.

phases.name: Governance gate — retire founding goal G2 (OPERATOR ACTION, BLOCKING)
phases.description: founding-goals.md declares itself the one artifact agents may not author or amend; retiring a goal requires a human commit with CODEOWNERS approval plus a Retirement-ADR. G2 (Multi-host scaleout) states the direct opposite of this workplan. No agent may edit that file, and no deletion phase may begin until the human commit lands — otherwise the repository's governance layer contradicts its own head commit. If this commit never lands, the workplan halts here with the daemon tier intact and P0 already banked.

gate.command: git log --oneline -- founding-goals.md | head -1 && grep -c '^## G2' founding-goals.md | grep -q '^0$'

tasks.name: Human commit removing G2, referencing ADR-2608241500
tasks.description: OPERATOR ACTION — NOT AGENT-EXECUTABLE. gary removes the '## G2 — Multi-host scaleout' section from founding-goals.md in a commit under CODEOWNERS approval, with a message citing ADR-2608241500 as the Retirement-ADR. G1 (model tiering and independence) and G3 (hexagonal rigor at the workspace level) remain in force and are strengthened by this work — do not touch them. Any agent that modifies founding-goals.md violates S18 and the workplan must halt.

phases.name: Extract hex-infer — the only real engineering
phases.description: hex-exec currently loops back to the daemon for inference (direct_exec.rs:771, direct_react.rs:131 -> http://127.0.0.1:{port}/api/inference/complete). This is the sole coupling between the canonical loop and hex-nexus. Extract the provider adapters and routing into a library crate depending only on hex-core, reqwest and tokio. Extract, do not rewrite — the behavior is measured and the benchmark corpus is the oracle. The phase gate is behavioral and falsifies the entire plan if it fails.

gate.command: hex nexus stop && hex do run 'add a doc comment to the function' --file hex-exec/src/compress.rs --evidence 'cargo check -p hex-exec'

tasks.name: Create hex-infer crate implementing IInferencePort
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. hex-infer crate created (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/providers/mod.rs), added to workspace members. Deps: hex-core, reqwest(rustls-tls,json,stream), tokio, serde, serde_json, async-trait, thiserror, futures, tracing. `cargo check -p hex-infer` clean.

ORIGINAL: New workspace crate hex-infer. Dependencies: hex-core, reqwest (rustls-tls, json, stream), tokio, serde, serde_json — nothing else. Public surface is a `complete(req) -> Result<Completion>` library function behind hex_core::ports::inference::IInferencePort. hex-infer is the single enforcement point for founding goal G1: no consumer outside this crate and hex-core/src/ports/inference.rs may name a concrete provider (S16).

tasks.name: Move Ollama and claude-code adapters out of hex-nexus
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. ollama.rs (564) + claude_code.rs (500) git-mv'd to hex-infer/src/providers/. They had ZERO `crate::` references, so the move was verbatim — no axum/AppState coupling existed. hex-nexus/src/adapters/inference/mod.rs is now a re-export shim (deleted with the daemon in P5.2); hex-nexus depends on hex-infer. 5/5 moved unit tests pass; `cargo check --workspace --exclude hex-desktop` clean. STILL OPEN (carried to P2.4): the Ollama adapter does not forward max_tokens/temperature/num_ctx and its `grammar` field is dead against Ollama (real mechanism is `format` JSON-Schema). Deliberately deferred so the move stayed behaviour-preserving.

ORIGINAL: Relocate hex-nexus/src/adapters/inference/ollama.rs (564 LOC) and claude_code.rs (500 LOC) into hex-infer/src/providers/, stripping axum State and AppState coupling. Known defect to fix while moving (do not carry it forward): the Ollama adapter never forwards max_tokens, temperature or num_ctx, causing silent context starvation, and its `grammar` field is dead code against Ollama — the real mechanism is the `format` JSON-Schema field.

tasks.name: Salvage OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic adapters out of hex-agent
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. openai_compat.rs (582) and anthropic.rs (433) rewritten into hex-infer/src/providers/ against hex_core::ports::inference::IInferencePort, replacing hex-agent's private AnthropicPort. The domain types translated for free — hex-agent/src/domain/mod.rs re-exports hex_core::domain::messages, so ContentBlock/Message/Role/StopReason/ToolDefinition/RateLimitHeaders were already hex-core types under a different path. One provider abstraction now: 4 adapters, 1 trait.
Reconciliation: the OpenAI-compat adapter's ollama() constructor is kept but documented as the remote/shim path — local Ollama should use providers::ollama, which streams NDJSON for real.
Added hex-infer/src/providers/vec_stream.rs: hex_core defines its own minimal Stream trait (not futures), so buffered providers need a Vec-backed adapter to satisfy IInferencePort::stream.
FIXED IN THE MOVE (do not carry forward): (a) temperature is now forwarded by both adapters — the old AnthropicPort signature had no parameter for it, so it was silently dropped on every request; (b) the SSE parser dropped a trailing event when the stream did not end with a blank line; (c) Anthropic's message_delta now emits Usage + MessageStop separately, matching hex_core's StreamChunk shape; (d) both adapters gained health() probes (GET /models, GET /v1/models) that IInferencePort requires and AnthropicPort had no place for; (e) request timeouts are now set (HEX_INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_SECS, default 300s) — the originals used a default reqwest::Client with no timeout at all.
KNOWN GAP, deferred to P2.4: request.grammar is ignored by both. OpenAI-compat servers express structured output via response_format, Anthropic has no GBNF equivalent. Documented in the module headers rather than silently pretended.
The hex-agent originals were NOT deleted — hex-agent still wires them and the whole crate dies in P5.2. Both files now carry a SUPERSEDED header pointing at hex-infer so nobody patches the dead copy.
Evidence: cargo test -p hex-infer = 35 passed / 0 failed (was 5); cargo clippy -p hex-infer --all-targets -D clippy::correctness -D clippy::suspicious = clean; cargo check --workspace --exclude hex-desktop = clean.

ORIGINAL: Relocate hex-agent/src/adapters/secondary/openai_compat.rs (582 LOC) and anthropic.rs (433 LOC) into hex-infer/src/providers/. These are the only parts of hex-agent's 23,383 LOC worth keeping; the crate is deleted in P5.2 and nothing in the workspace depends on it. Reconcile any duplication with P2.2's adapters into one provider abstraction.

tasks.name: Lift inference_complete from axum handler to library function
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. inference_complete (routes/inference.rs:66-1099) lifted into hex-infer as a plain async fn complete(CompleteRequest, &InferenceConfig) -> Result<Completion, CompleteError>. New modules: config.rs (359), endpoint.rs (246), routing.rs (425), transport.rs (830), complete.rs. hex-infer is now 5,422 LOC / 108 tests.

THE 18 STATE READS WERE NOT 18 UNKNOWNS. Counted and grouped: 5 inference_stdb (registry + logging), 4 rate_limiter, 3 spacetime_secrets (vault), 5 openrouter/anthropic api keys, 2 fingerprints. The ADR already drops the first three groups (12 reads); the key reads are env lookups wearing a disguise; only fingerprints needed a decision.

KEY FINDING — NO MIGRATION NEEDED. ~/.hex/inference-servers.json already exists and is already authoritative: hex-nexus/src/config_sync.rs:151 PRELOADS SpacetimeDB from that file on every startup (ADR-2026-04-08-0813). The database was downstream of the file all along. hex-cli calls it a 'cache' (inference.rs:315) but the dataflow says otherwise. Severing STDB costs no data and needs no schema invention — hex-infer reads the same file the daemon read.

LAYERING CHANGE (not a drop): ACI fingerprint injection (ADR-2026-03-30-1200) moved from a State read to CompleteRequest::aci_block, supplied by the caller. Context assembly is hex-exec/hex-graph's job — context quality is the stated differentiator of the single-loop thesis — and hex-infer's job is to place the call. hex-infer no longer needs a fingerprint store to know what a fingerprint is.

VAULT -> ENV: Endpoint::resolve_secret reads the env var the apiKeyRef names. The daemon ran a SpacetimeDB vault lookup under a 3s timeout with three distinct abort branches; for one user on one machine that is a distributed system standing in for std::env::var. Removes a network hop, a timeout, and the whole secret_resolution_failed error class, and keeps keys out of every file hex writes.

QUANT ROUTER: not ported wholesale. quant_router.rs (324) + complexity.rs (152) classified prompt complexity to pick a minimum weight-quantisation tier — useful when a fleet chose among many cloud providers, dead weight when the solo agent names its model via explicit tier routing. The ORDERING it applied is kept in routing::pick_default (local -> healthy -> highest benchmarked qualityScore), reading qualityScore straight out of the registry file. Recorded here rather than silently dropped.

RETAINED as the ADR requires: tier routing (routing::tier_for_strategy/tier_model), the full fallback chain (tools fast-path -> matched endpoint -> cloud retry / local backoff+jitter / rate-limit sleep -> registered :free providers -> free-model chain on a bare key -> any local endpoint -> Anthropic direct), 401 as a hard non-retryable failure, and the exact wire shape simple_agent.rs parses (Completion::to_json, guarded by a test).
DROPPED as the ADR requires: LoRA attach (lora_attach::resolve_serving_model), the STDB inference_log write, the rate limiter (4 reads), the /v1 proxy shims, calibration endpoints.

DEDUPLICATION: provider_supports_tools/priority_for_tools existed as free fns in the lifted transport AND as Endpoint methods. The free fns were deleted; Endpoint is the single source of truth.

BEST-OF-N: no work needed here. It already lives on the correct side of the seam — hex-exec/src/direct_react.rs::react_execute_best_of_n, called from direct_exec.rs:399 (ADR-2606072044). The ADR's 'RETAIN best-of-N with compile gate' is satisfied by leaving it where it is; hex-infer/src/best_of_n.rs is NOT needed and the file list for this task is corrected accordingly.

NOT DONE HERE (P2.5's job): the nexus handler still runs its own copy; hex-exec still calls the loopback. Swapping both is P2.5, and Completion::to_json makes that swap parser-transparent.

Evidence: cargo test -p hex-infer = 108 passed / 0 failed (was 35); cargo clippy -p hex-infer --all-targets -D clippy::correctness -D clippy::suspicious = clean; cargo check --workspace --exclude hex-desktop = clean.

ORIGINAL: hex-nexus/src/routes/inference.rs::inference_complete spans lines 66-1099 (1,033 LOC) and performs 18 State(...) reads. Lift it into hex-infer as a plain function; configuration comes from .hex/project.json (inference.tier_models, inference.react_models), where it is already declared. RETAIN: tier routing, best-of-N with compile gate, claude -p frontier fallback, the tool fast-path response shape hex-exec/src/simple_agent.rs:724 depends on. DROP: LoRA augmentation (ADR-2606161300 is Proposed, not built), STDB inference logging, the rate limiter, the /v1 OpenAI and Anthropic proxy shims, calibration endpoints. This is the highest-risk task in the workplan — the 18 State reads are the only genuine unknown.

tasks.name: Repoint hex-exec off the HTTP loopback
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. New module hex-exec/src/infer.rs wraps hex_infer::complete behind complete_json(Value) -> Result<Value,String>, keeping the exact JSON request/response shapes the daemon endpoint used — which is why no tool-call parser changed. Three loopback sites repointed, not two: direct_exec.rs::request_edit, direct_react.rs (the ReAct turn AND summarize_overflow, which the task text missed), and simple_agent.rs::run, whose `inference_url: String` parameter is gone from the signature. Its only caller, hex-nexus/src/routes/agent_run.rs, was updated and HEX_AGENT_INFERENCE_URL is dead. hex-infer added to hex-exec deps. 3 contract tests added; 92 hex-exec lib tests pass; `cargo check --workspace` clean. `hex do` is now fully in-process: no daemon, no localhost hop.

ORIGINAL: Replace the two loopback call sites (hex-exec/src/direct_exec.rs:771 and direct_react.rs:131) with in-process calls through IInferencePort backed by hex-infer. Add hex-infer to hex-exec's dependencies. hex-cli already depends on hex-exec directly and does NOT depend on hex-nexus, so `hex do` becomes a fully in-process call with no daemon hop. Satisfies S01.

phases.name: Sever SpacetimeDB from hex-exec
phases.description: hex-exec has no spacetimedb-sdk dependency — its 8 touchpoints are plain HTTP SQL calls behind HEX_SPACETIMEDB_HOST, so this is a store swap rather than surgery. `cargo check -p hex-nexus --no-default-features` already returns 0 errors, proving the seam holds.

gate.command: ! grep -rn --include='*.rs' -i spacetime hex-exec/src | grep -v '^\s*//' | grep -q . && cargo check --workspace

tasks.name: Add a LocalStore port and file-backed adapter
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. Port at hex-core/src/ports/local_store.rs (ILocalStore + RunRecord/UsageRecord/EmissionRecord/MemoryEntry). Adapter at hex-exec/src/store/mod.rs (FileStore), JSONL not SQLite — the volumes are a 2,000-run ring buffer and a few hundred ~500-byte notes, and JSONL needs no new dependency, no schema and no migration. The trait is SYNCHRONOUS: every operation is a small local file read, so making it async would oblige hex-core to take a position on a runtime for no benefit. 16 adapter tests.

ORIGINAL: Define a narrow port in hex-core for the small amount of state hex-exec actually persists: the agent-run feed, cost-meter totals, and ADR/spec/workplan emission records. Back it with SQLite at ~/.hex/hex.db or append-only JSONL. This replaces the STDB HTTP SQL surface, including the ORDER BY workaround at direct_exec.rs:276 (STDB SQL has no ORDER BY, so results were fetched bounded and sorted in Rust — a real store makes that unnecessary).

tasks.name: Repoint the 8 STDB call sites
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. All 8 STDB call sites repointed; `grep HEX_SPACETIMEDB_HOST|HEX_STDB_HOST|SPACETIME_URL hex-exec/src` is now empty.

THE FIVE EMITTERS CHANGED BEHAVIOUR, DELIBERATELY. adr_draft/spec_draft/workplan_emit/adr_status_set/code_patch used to POST a proposed_action_open row and return 'queued; the digital-twin executor will write the file after approval'. The twin and the executor are inside hex-nexus. Once it is deleted, a tool that only queues does nothing while telling the model it succeeded — the worst available outcome. New shared helper hex-exec/src/tools/emit.rs writes the file and records the emission. Nothing is ungoverned: the approval that mattered was never the twin's auto-approve (it rubber-stamped anything tagged tool:*) but direct_exec's evidence gate, which is untouched.

THE COST METER HAD NO WRITER. It read inference_log, a table the daemon wrote; P2.4 dropped that logging. Fixed at the source: hex-exec/src/infer.rs::complete now takes (caller, intent) and appends a UsageRecord after every completion, so the meter reads what the loop actually spent. All four call sites tagged.

BUGS FOUND AND FIXED IN THE MOVE: (a) code_patch resolved its repo root from HEX_REPO_ROOT defaulting to the hardcoded string "/home/gary/hex-intf" — on any other machine it wrote outside the repository; now one resolution in emit::repo_root(). (b) escalate_to_operator built an STDB reducer URL and threw it away with `let _ = url`, so an escalation reached the operator only if they read the daemon log; it now writes an EmissionRecord.

STILL OPEN, recorded for P4.1: hex-exec/src/tools/delegate.rs POSTs to /api/org/send-message — pure org-sim residue, dead in the solo model. Deletion belongs with the rest of the org-sim in P5.5, not here.

ORIGINAL: Replace HEX_SPACETIMEDB_HOST / SPACETIME_URL / HEX_STDB_HOST usage in hex-exec/src/tools/{code_patch.rs:235, adr_draft.rs:114, spec_draft.rs:103, workplan_emit.rs:200, adr_status_set.rs:147, escalate_to_operator.rs:67, cost_meter.rs:72} and hex-exec/src/direct_exec.rs:226 with LocalStore calls. Verify the agent-run feed still hydrates and `hex do runs` still lists prior runs. Satisfies S08.

tasks.name: File-backed memory store — replace the hexflo_memory STDB table
tasks.description:
DONE 2026-09-11. Memory is Markdown files with YAML frontmatter under .hex/memory/ (git-tracked — .gitignore gained `!.hex/memory/` under the `**/.hex/*` rule) and ~/.hex/memory/ (cross-project). Project scope shadows global on the same key. Three read sites repointed: hex-exec/src/tools/memory_search.rs (same result shape, so the model sees an identical object), direct_exec::fetch_lessons, and hex-cli/src/commands/memory/. The rank_lessons seam was already cut and needed no change.

CLI: store/get/search kept and repointed, list/delete added (trivial now), and `store` gained --global. REMOVED sync-check and validate: both existed only to prove two agents on two hosts saw the same STDB row. With one agent and one machine that is not a property any more, and S15 forbids leaving a verb to fail at runtime.

FIXED IN THE MOVE: `hex memory search` sliced its preview by byte index (`&value[..57]`), which panics on any multi-byte character; it now clips on a character boundary, with a test.

OPERATOR NOTE: SpacetimeDB is not running and returns nothing, so no lessons were migrated. If the database holds lessons worth keeping, start it and export hexflo_memory BEFORE P5.3 deletes spacetime-modules/.

ORIGINAL: RESOLVES A CONFLICT IN THIS WORKPLAN (raised by the operator 2026-09-11): P6.2 and spec S04 require the loop to keep returning graph-proximity-ranked lessons from a 'local lesson store', but P6.1 lists the `memory` verb among the CLI verbs to delete and names no replacement. P6.1 is amended to KEEP `hex memory`, re-backed by files.

Memory today is the hexflo_memory STDB table (key, value, scope, updated_at) under four key prefixes: lesson:, gap:, project:, decision: — ~500 bytes per entry. That is not database-shaped.

Store: one Markdown file per entry with YAML frontmatter (key, scope, updated_at) under .hex/memory/ (project-scoped, git-tracked) and ~/.hex/memory/ (cross-project). Committing lessons to the repo is a net gain over STDB: lessons become reviewable in git diff, they travel with a clone, two machines share memory through git, and they survive an STDB wipe. No index — a few hundred small files scan in microseconds and rank_lessons does the real selection.

THE SEAM IS ALREADY CUT: hex_graph::context::rank_lessons(&ContextBundle, &[(String,String)], limit) takes plain pairs and has no store coupling. Only the feed changes, at three call sites: hex-exec/src/tools/memory_search.rs:86 (GET /api/hexflo/memory/search), hex-exec/src/direct_exec.rs:675, and hex-nexus/src/routes/graph.rs:247 (dies with the daemon). hex-cli/src/commands/memory/mod.rs:72/91/117 repoint from NexusClient to the same store.

The memory_search tool keeps its name, description and input schema exactly — the prompt contract must not change, or every persona's GROUND phase behaviour shifts underneath the P9.1 benchmark comparison.

Fold the read/write surface into P3.1's ILocalStorePort rather than adding a second port; it is the same 'small durable facts' concern.

phases.name: Consumer trace and test salvage — before any deletion
phases.description: ADR-2026-04-05-0900 records hex-agent being broken for an entire session because one workplan deleted code whose feature-gated importers were never traced. This phase exists so that failure cannot repeat, and so that 1,683 tests are not deleted wholesale. Nothing is removed here.

tasks.name: Build the consumer dependency map for every deletion target
tasks.description: Run `hex graph consumers` (ADR-2606071713) across the ENTIRE workspace for every crate, module and asset slated for deletion in P5-P7: hex-nexus, hex-agent, hex-desktop, hex-state, spacetime-modules, hex-cli/src/pipeline, hex-cli/src/tui, hex-nexus/src/orchestration/agent_loop, hex-cli/assets/wasm, the 16 org-sim YAMLs, and each hex-core port and domain type listed in P7. tasks.name: Port surviving tests forward into the crates they exercise

Identify every test whose assertions concern hex-exec, hex-core, hex-analysis, hex-graph or hex-git rather than daemon routing, and relocate it into that crate's own test module or tests/ directory, confirming it passes there. Tests that only exercise daemon routing, STDB adapters, or the dashboard are deleted with them — record the deleted count explicitly rather than letting it vanish silently. Satisfies S06.

phases.name: Delete the daemon tier
phases.description: The irreversible phase. Every task ends with `cargo check --workspace` before the next begins — a 'done' phase with a broken build is worse than no phase. Order matters: hex-desktop and hex-agent first (nothing depends on them), then hex-nexus, then the CLI-internal modules.

tasks.name: Delete hex-agent (23,383 LOC)
tasks.description: Nothing in the workspace depends on hex-agent — it is a third agent loop with its own conversation usecase and provider adapters, superseded by hex-exec. Its two useful adapters were salvaged in P2.3. Remove the directory and its [workspace] members entry.

tasks.description:
Remove: sched + sched/ (10,122), mcp (1,794), persona_prompt (1,276 — org-sim residue), report (1,237), nexus (1,216), stdb (1,090), adr_review (992 — merge its linting into adr/), project (705), substrate (664 — Layer-6 composition-swap governance), enforce (584 — or make file-local), opencode (549), chat (546), neural_lab (518), and ops, secrets, monitor, trust, task, taste, inbox, pool, insight, sandbox, pulse, fingerprint, context, steer, pause, decide, override, deploy, interview, agent_audit, refresh, plan_health (~7,700 combined). AMENDED 2026-09-11: `memory` is REMOVED from this delete list. P6.2 and spec S04 require a local lesson store; deleting the only verb that writes to it would make S04 unsatisfiable. `hex memory` survives, re-backed by files per P3.3.

tasks.name: Repoint surviving verbs from NexusClient to in-process calls
tasks.description: The kept verbs (do, analyze, graph, bench, inference, verify, dev, ci, test, init, new, worktree, git, fs, docs, spec, assets, skill, self-update, status, go, hey, readme, plan/, adr/, doctor/, bootstrap/) currently call the daemon over HTTP. Replace NexusClient usage with direct library calls into hex-exec, hex-analysis, hex-graph, hex-git and hex-infer. Delete hex-cli/src/nexus_client.rs (625 LOC). The `hex graph` verb and hex-exec's context assembly must keep returning code-graph-relevant context and graph-proximity-ranked lessons from the local graph-out/graph.json and local lesson store, with no network call — context quality is the stated differentiator of the single-loop thesis (S04).

tasks.name: Trim inference, plan and adr verbs of daemon-era bulk
tasks.description: inference.rs 3,348 -> ~1,500: drop the Queue, Stats, EscalationReport, QReport, Usage, Discovered, Corpus and Adapter{register,list,remove,disable,enable,evaluate} subcommands (STDB telemetry and unbuilt LoRA); keep Add, List, Test, Discover, Remove, Setup, Bench, GpuCheck. plan/ 5,038 -> ~3,900: reconcile.rs (644) and reconcile_evidence.rs (479) exist to resync workplan state with daemon-run agents; in-process the executor knows its own result. adr/doctor.rs 2,398 -> ~1,400: keep structural linting, drop STDB-synced status machinery. Also resolve the 27 #[allow(dead_code)] sites in hex-cli.

tasks.name: Rename hex swarm build/review to hex build/harden
tasks.description: The cooperative+adversarial harness (hex-exec/src/adversarial.rs, 475 LOC) is in-process fan-out of inference calls — no registry, no heartbeats, no peers — and is the measured source of quality (it built a ~2,900-LOC durable job queue from a one-line spec and found 6 real bugs the build's own passing tests missed). Retain the implementation unchanged; rename the verbs so 'swarm' stops implying a cluster that no longer exists. Keep --gate semantics: the test command is the only authority. Satisfies S05.

tasks.name: Fold hex-analyzer into hex-analysis
tasks.description: Merge hex-analyzer's six analyzers (composition_churn 441, cohesion 404, duplication 383, god_types 370, dead_layer 328, orphan 325) into hex-analysis, which already owns tree-sitter boundary checking, the layer classifier, dead-export detection and ADR conformance. One analysis crate, one entry point. Rule identity and severity must not change — S03 is the regression check.

phases.name: Trim hex-core to a contract surface
phases.description: hex-core is the gravity center — every crate depends on it — so it is trimmed last, once its consumers are gone. ~5,400 of 8,520 LOC dies with the daemon. It must keep zero runtime dependencies; that is the G3 test.

gate.command: cargo check --workspace && cargo tree -p hex-core --edges normal --prefix none | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u | wc -l

phases.name: Prove it
phases.description: The workplan is not done because the code compiles. ADR-2608241500 is falsifiable at this gate: no benchmark regression, an A-or-better self-analysis, a real build from a one-line spec, and an adversarial pass over the whole diff. The skill's own rule applies — a migration with more than 5 deletion steps gets an explicit adversarial-reviewer step, and this one has 16.

gate.command: hex bench agentic && hex analyze . && cargo test --workspace

tasks.name: Benchmark against the P0 baseline
tasks.description: Re-run `hex bench agentic` over docs/benchmarks/ and compare per-model pass-rates against docs/benchmarks/baseline-2608241500.json. Any decrease for any model in inference.react_models is a blocking failure requiring root-cause before the workplan can be marked done. External leaderboard scores are inadmissible here — ADR-2606071734 measured the top-leaderboard local model scoring last on this grid. Satisfies S02. Also assert S04 directly: the loop's context assembly still sources graph context and ranked lessons locally, with no daemon and no network call.

tasks.name: Self-analysis must score A or better
tasks.description: Run `hex analyze .` over the surviving workspace. nexus scored F (30/100) against hex's own analyzer before its crate split; a 49k-LOC single binary that sells hexagonal rigor has no excuse for failing the rules it enforces on others. Verify the G3 conditions directly: hex-core pulls only zero-runtime crates, no adapter crate imports another adapter crate, and hex-cli is the only composition root. Satisfies S03.

tasks.name: Build a real project end-to-end from a one-line spec
tasks.description: Run `hex build '<one-line challenge>' --target <dir> --gate '<test command>'` followed by `hex harden` against a fresh target — the lru-clean or ratelimiter-clean fixture class. Confirm the design/red-team/synthesize/implement chain still reaches a passing gate, and that the harden pass still surfaces bugs the build's own tests missed. This is the product claim; it must be demonstrated, not asserted. Satisfies S05.

tasks.name: Adversarial review of the entire collapse diff
tasks.description: Run the adversarial reviewer over the full diff from the P0 base commit to HEAD, with lenses tuned to this specific failure mode: silently dropped behavior (a feature-gated import missed, a tested guarantee deleted with no replacement), tests deleted rather than ported, provider names leaking outside hex-infer (S16), and any surviving code path that would attempt a daemon connection (S15). Verify each of S01-S18 explicitly and record the verdict. Default to refute.
